title: A Familiar Face in the Doorway

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay. I think I'm actually ready to sign tomorrow."

options.text: Good — the Fool, the Lovers, and the Empress are all working together now.
That just means something new is about to fall apart.
That means you should still be protecting this quietly, not signing anything.

elaboration: That's the whole point of doing a reading like this together, instead of one card at a time — you get to see where all three actually agree.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: As Dave gets up to leave, someone else is already waiting by the door.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Oh — hey. You're the guy who was in here forever."

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: There's a beat. You look between them, and can't help yourself.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: They say it in perfect unison, then both look a little embarrassed about how fast that was.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I just mentioned I've been building furniture. She needs stage risers for the tour."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Turns out 'sturdy' and 'won't collapse on a drummer' is harder to find than you'd think."

options.text: Sounds like a good partnership — no card required to see that.
Furniture and tours have nothing to do with each other.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Wait, isn't this basically a Lovers moment — two people, one choice to work together?"

options.text: Sort of — but the Lovers is about a choice you're facing, not two people meeting.
Yes, exactly — the card's about you two specifically.
No, the Lovers only ever means romance.

elaboration: The card was never about who shows up in the doorway — it's about the choice itself, and you two each already made a different one, on different days, for different reasons.
